A [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] '''Imperial Advisor''' was a member of the [[Imperial Ruling Council/Legends|Ruling Council]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. One of only a few hundred [[Imperial Advisor/Legends|Advisors]] who were genuinely loyal to [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Galactic Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] and a high-ranking [[Bureaucrat/Legends|bureaucrat]], the [[Advisor/Legends|Advisor]] wore lavish light [[Color/Legends|blue]] robes and a tall, dark blue hat. In [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], the tall-hatted Advisor accompanied the [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] to the [[Endor system/Legends|Endor system]] and arrived aboard the [[Death Star II/Legends|second Death Star]], an Imperial [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]] that was undergoing construction. Alongside five other members of the Ruling Council, the tall-hatted Advisor followed the Emperor as he disembarked his [[Emperor's personal shuttle/Legends|private shuttle]] and was greeted by a large gathering of [[Imperial officer/Legends|Imperial officers]] and [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]]. However, the [[Space station/Legends|station]] was [[Battle of Endor/Legends|destroyed]] by the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] a few days later, and all six Advisors were [[Death/Legends|killed]].

==Biography==
A [[Human/Legends|Human]]<ref name="Starships" /> [[Gender/Legends|male]]<ref name="mistaken identity" /> served the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] as an [[Imperial Advisor/Legends|Imperial Advisor]] during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. Of the several thousand [[Advisor/Legends|Advisors]] who ran [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Galactic Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine's]] [[Bureaucrat/Legends|bureaucracy]], the Advisor was one of only a few hundred who demonstrated genuine loyalty to the [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] and his [[New Order/Legends|New Order]]. Those individuals were consequently appointed to the [[Imperial Ruling Council/Legends|Imperial Ruling Council]], also known as the Emperor's Inner Circle. Based on the [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] [[Capital/Legends|capital]] [[Planet/Legends|world]] of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]],<ref name="Starships" /> the members of the Ruling Council were permitted private audiences with the Emperor.<ref name="Barbarian" /> Their duties were to manage the Empire and carry out the Emperor's will.<ref name="Character Encyclopedia">''[[Star Wars Character Encyclopedia]]''</ref>

Palpatine encouraged competition between his Advisors, tasking them with overseeing not only their home [[Star system/Legends|systems]] but those of rival Advisors as well.<ref name="Character Encyclopedia" /> He thus kept them loyal to him while discouraging internal cooperation and alliances between them.<ref name="Galaxy Guide 5">[[Galaxy Guide 5: Return of the Jedi (Second Edition)|''Galaxy Guide 5: Return of the Jedi'', Second Edition]]</ref>

To further promote suspicion among his Advisors, the Emperor doted on only a select few at any given [[Time/Legends|time]].<ref name="Galaxy Guide 5" /> In [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]],<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> the tall-hatted Advisor was one of six<ref name="Return of the Jedi" /> Inner Circle members<ref name="Barbarian" /> who accompanied Palpatine to the [[Death Star II/Legends|second Death Star]], a massive Imperial [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]] under construction in the [[Endor system/Legends|Endor system]]. The group arrived aboard the [[Space station/Legends|station]] in the Emperor's [[Emperor's personal shuttle/Legends|private shuttle]] and, flanked by Palpatine's [[Emperor's Royal Guard/Legends|Royal Guard]], disembarked into a [[Hangar/Legends|hangar]] crowded with a welcoming assembly of [[Imperial officer/Legends|Imperial officers]] and [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]]. The Emperor was greeted by his [[Sith apprentice/Legends|Sith apprentice]], [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]], and as the two departed the hangar, the Advisors silently followed in their wake. A short time later, the [[Death Star/Legends|station]] was destroyed during an [[Battle of Endor/Legends|attack]] by the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] [[Alliance Fleet/Legends|fleet]],<ref name="Return of the Jedi" /> and all six Advisors<ref name="Kren Blista-Vanee Galactic File Card" />&mdash;as well as both Vader and the Emperor&mdash;were [[Death/Legends|killed]].<ref name="Return of the Jedi" />

==Personality and traits==
The Advisor had pale skin and [[Color/Legends|brown]] eyebrows.<ref name="Barbarian" />

==Equipment==
High-ranking advisors often wore lavish robes indicative of their status,<ref name="Character Encyclopedia" /> and the Advisor wore a light blue robe with a piece of tall, dark blue headwear.<ref name="Starships" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|The Emperor's Inner Circle, or Palpatine's creepy advisors, depending on your point-of-view&hellip;|Keeper of the [[Holocron continuity database|Holocron]] [[Leland Chee]], describing a picture of the tall-hatted Advisor and four of the other Inner Circle members who appear in ''Return of the Jedi''|<ref name="Barbarian" />}}
[[File:EmperorsArrival-SWHC10.png|thumb|left|325px|The tall-hatted Advisor's lone scene in ''Return of the Jedi'']]
The tall-hatted Advisor was one of six who followed the Emperor onto the second Death Star in [[Richard Marquand]]'s [[1983]] film, [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']].<ref name="Return of the Jedi" /> The tall-hatted Advisor's outfit was inspired by [[Wikipedia:Catholic Church|Catholic]] [[Wikipedia:Bishop|bishops]], whom the film's assistant art director, [[Nilo Rodis-Jamero]], looked to when designing the robes and elaborate headgear of all of the Advisors.<ref name="Annotated Screenplays">''[[Star Wars: The Annotated Screenplays]]''</ref> In concept art of the arrival scene by artist [[Ralph McQuarrie]], tall hats are worn by two different Imperial digitaries, neither of whom are dressed in blue.<ref name="Art of Ralph McQuarrie">''[[The Art of Ralph McQuarrie]]''</ref>

Prior to ''Return of the Jedi''{{'s}} release, the arrival scene was described in [[James Kahn]]'s [[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (novelization)|novelization]] of the film, in which Kahn refers to the group as "the Emperor's courtiers."<ref name="novel">[[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode VI: Return of the Jedi'' novelization]]</ref> The character's death aboard the Death Star was not revealed until the ''[[2013 Topps Star Wars Galactic Files Series 2]]'' card set.<ref name="Kren Blista-Vanee Galactic File Card" />

In [[2003]], a production photo of five of the six Advisors seen in ''Return of the Jedi'' was included in an [https://web.archive.org/web/20031008010828/www.starwars.com/community/askjc/jocasta/askjc20030602.html article] published on [[StarWars.com]], accompanied by text that read: "Among the members of Palpatine's Inner Circle are: [[Sate Pestage/Legends|Sate Pestage]], [[Janus Greejatus/Legends|Janus Greejatus]], [[Sim Aloo/Legends|Sim Aloo]], [[Ars Dangor/Legends|Ars Dangor]], and [[Kren Blista-Vanee/Legends|Kren Blista-Vanee]]."<ref name="mistaken identity" /> At that time, three of the Advisors in the photo had already been identified in the [[Star Wars Legends|Expanded Universe]] as Greejatus,<ref name="Greejatus">{{CCG|set=Death Star II Limited|cardname=Janus Greejatus}}</ref> Aloo,<ref name="Aloo">{{CCG|set=Death Star II Limited|cardname=Sim Aloo}}</ref> and Blista-Vanee,<ref name="Blista-Vanee">''[[Galaxy Guide 5: Return of the Jedi]]''</ref> but neither the tall-hatted Advisor nor the black-robed fifth Advisor had been named.

As Sate Pestage, a pre-existing Expanded Universe character, had been visually depicted sporting headwear similar to that worn by the fifth Advisor,<ref name="Pestage">''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref> the StarWars.com article led to some fan beliefs that the tall-hatted Advisor was Dangor.<ref name="confusion2">{{Blog|teekay-421|66|Deciphering CCG Imperials on Death Star II}}</ref> Contradicting this idea was an illustration of Dangor from [[1997]]'s ''[[Star Wars Trilogy Sourcebook, Special Edition]]'', which did not resemble any of the Advisors seen in the photo,<ref name="Trilogy Sourcebook">''[[Star Wars Trilogy Sourcebook, Special Edition]]''</ref> as well as several sources which established that Dangor lived past the Battle of Endor.<ref name="Dark Empire Sourcebook">''[[Dark Empire Sourcebook]]''</ref><ref name="Cracken's Threat Dossier">''[[Cracken's Threat Dossier]]''</ref> However, the rebooted ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[Canon|continuity]] reconciled the two characters and firmly established that the tall-hatted Advisor was in fact Ars Dangor.<ref name="Kernels and Husks">{{StoryCite|story=Kernels and Husks|book=From a Certain Point of View: Return of the Jedi}}</ref>
